concepts.def: Places in town: la biblioteca (library), el ayuntamiento (town hall), la piscina (swimming pool), la tienda (shop).
'Hay' means 'there is / there are': En mi barrio hay un parque pero no hay cine.
Directions: sigue todo recto (carry straight on), gira a la derecha (turn right), está al lado de (it is next to).
'Se puede' + infinitive means 'you can': En mi pueblo se puede ir de compras (In my town you can go shopping).
Pros and cons of an area: lo bueno es que es tranquilo (the good thing is it's quiet), lo malo es que hay mucho ruido (lots of noise).
Neighbourhood vocab: las afueras (outskirts), el centro (centre), la zona peatonal (pedestrian zone), los vecinos (neighbours).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Theme 3: My Neighbourhood — a core area of GCSE Spanish.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Theme 3: My Neighbourhood brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Theme 3: My Neighbourhood.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: In my neighbourhood there is a beach.

My neighbour has a swimming pool.
In my neighbourhood there is a swimming pool.

the bank

mcqs.q: Which is correct for 'The cinema is next to the park'?
